summary: This EOB shows a specialist visit and lab test on June 9, 2026. Your plan paid most of the allowed amounts, and you owe a $50 copay for the specialist visit plus $24 coinsurance (your percentage share) for the lab. The provider wrote off the difference between their bill and the plan's contracted rate.

lines.explanation: Specialist office visit: You paid a $50 copay. This is a fixed amount for a covered specialist visit (PLAN-COPAY: "Office visit copays are $25 for primary care and $50 for specialists"). The plan paid $95 toward the allowed amount of $145. The provider's bill was $260, but they agreed to accept $145 with the plan; the extra $115 is written off (CODE-CO-45: "the difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care").

citations.quote: PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service
Office visit copays are $25 for primary care and $50 for specialists
Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care

lines.explanation: Lab test (metabolic panel): After your deductible was already met, you owe $24 coinsurance. This is your percentage share of the allowed amount (CODE-PR-2: "coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met"). The plan paid $96 and you pay $24 of the $120 allowed. The provider's bill was $240, but the agreed rate is $120; the extra $120 is written off (CODE-CO-45: "the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan").

citations.quote: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met
CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider

actions: Review the itemized bill from Bayview Endocrinology Associates to verify the visit date (June 9, 2026) and service descriptions match this EOB.
When you receive a bill from the provider, confirm it only requests the $50 copay and $24 coinsurance shown here—not the written-off amounts.
Check your plan documents to confirm your coinsurance percentage (appears to be 20% based on the $24 share of $120 allowed).
